usage: nightshift start [-h] [--prompt-file PROMPT_FILE] [--cwd CWD]
                        [--no-worktree] [--target-branch TARGET_BRANCH]
                        [--continue-from SHIFT_DIR] [--crew CREW] [--dry-run]
                        [prompt]

Start a Nightshift crew: Claude Foreman, Advisor, Coder and Tester side by
side in one Windows Terminal tab (the default crew; --crew NAME uses
crews/NAME.yaml for other roles and pane counts). The task is saved to
<state_dir>/prompt.txt and given to Foreman only; Coder and Tester send READY
and wait for Foreman to delegate work; the Advisor stays dormant until Foreman
consults it. Git shifts use an isolated worktree; --no-worktree keeps in-place
execution. Each start is a new shift with its own <shift>-foreman /
<shift>-advisor / <shift>-coder / <shift>-tester session names; there is no
restart or resume, and a closed pane is not relaunched. A folder holds one
live shift at a time: start exits with code 3 while another live shift holds
the working folder (nightshift down releases it).

positional arguments:
  prompt                the task for Foreman (quote it; it is treated as plain
                        text), or a ticket ID such as NGH-005: the ticket body
                        becomes the task and its codebase: field the working
                        folder

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --prompt-file PROMPT_FILE
                        read the task from this UTF-8 file instead (safest for
                        text with quotes or & | < > ^ %)
  --cwd CWD             folder the crew works in (default: the ticket
                        codebase, else the current directory)
  --no-worktree         work in place with the existing folder lock
  --target-branch TARGET_BRANCH
                        branch to start from and land onto (repository
                        default, else main)
  --continue-from SHIFT_DIR
                        an earlier shift folder for the same task: its
                        handover.md is appended so the crew carries on
  --crew CREW           crew manifest crews/CREW.yaml: roles, briefs, colours,
                        counts, model (default: default = one Foreman, one
                        Advisor, one Coder, one Tester)
  --dry-run             print the intended command, roles and prompt as JSON;
                        launch and write nothing

Example: nightshift start "Add a --verbose flag to report.py" | nightshift
start --dry-run --prompt-file task.txt

usage: nightshift.exe [-h] [--live] [--brief-file BRIEF_FILE]

Nightshift launcher: one Windows Terminal tab, Foreman, Advisor, Coder and Tester side by side.

`start "task"` persists the task to
<state_dir>/prompt.txt and starts interactive Claude Foreman, Advisor, Coder and Tester (the default crew;
Opus 5.5, the Advisor Fable 5.1) in the "Nightshift Crew" Terminal profile (Cascadia Mono 12, dark). Only Foreman
receives the task; Coder and Tester get their role and peer identity, send READY and await work; the Advisor
(NGH-027) stays dormant until Foreman consults it, and the mailbox lets only Foreman address it. The task
reaches the panes by file path only, never as argv text. Panes run in the
shift's isolated git worktree (or the caller's directory with --no-worktree) in Claude's auto permission
mode (--permission-mode auto). Each `start` is a new shift: mesh names are
<shift>-foreman / <shift>-advisor / <shift>-coder / <shift>-tester, pane titles are '<ticket or shift> <Role>' (e.g. 'NGH-019 Foreman'), a loop
window is titled 'Nightshift <first ticket>..<last ticket>', and
<state_dir>/<Role>.json records pid, name, peer and model. There is no restart or
resume; a closed pane is not relaunched. `start --dry-run` prints the plan as
JSON without launching or writing anything.
Container (NGH-025): a crew with layout 2x4 (8 slots, 2 rows x 4 columns) or 1x4 (4 equal columns) puts the crew
in the first slots and plain cmd shells in the rest (each records <state_dir>/slots/<N>.json); the launcher exits once every pane and slot has
reported. `spawn SHIFT --role ROLE [--cli claude|gemini|codex|copilot] [--crew NAME] [--slot N]` starts a session in a free
slot of that window (Foreman's only way to add a crew member; --crew takes the role from crews/NAME.yaml), and Foreman ends its own shift with `down` (--close, the
default, closes the window; --hold keeps the tab). Git shifts use per-shift worktrees and a short
repository lock during `land`; direct and non-git working folders hold one live shift at a time.
`down` removes landed worktrees or preserves unlanded work on a recovery branch.
Coders claim files before editing them (`claim`/`release`/`claims`, kept in <state_dir>/claims.json); a file
held by another role makes `claim` exit 4 and change nothing.
Crew messages go through a durable mailbox (<state_dir>/mailbox.sqlite3): `msg send`/`msg sent`, `inbox`, `ack` (exit 5 = protocol violation).
Every mailbox row and the start/spawn/result/down events are appended to <state_dir>/bus.jsonl (the shift bus, a
plain file with no process); `log SHIFT [--follow] [--since N] [--json]` prints it in order.
`build` runs heavy builds one at a time per folder (exit 6 = waited past --timeout) and records <state_dir>/builds/<n>.json.
`resume` reruns, through `loop`, every ticket whose latest shift never reached done, continuing from that shift.
Result ladder: result.json carries a stage (implemented < tested < deployed < validated; none = implemented).
A ticket line `requires: <rung>` sets the bar (default tested); a done below it is recorded as 'short' and stops the loop.
The crew comes from a YAML manifest: crews/default.yaml unless `start --crew NAME` picks
crews/NAME.yaml (roles, brief files, colours, counts, model, permission mode; 2-8 panes,
one row up to 4, two rows above). A role with count > 1 gets labels Role-1..N and names <shift>-role-N.
Legacy modes: no args = placeholder layout; --live = ping/pong communication trial.
WT separators are native argv, not shell chaining. No software installs.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --live                diagnostic ping/pong communication trial with live
                        agents
  --brief-file BRIEF_FILE
                        with --live: replace the trial brief with this
                        assignment file

Commands:
  start "task"|TICKET [--dry-run] [--cwd D] [--crew NAME]
                                              start a crew (git worktree by default; --no-worktree opts out)
  land SHIFT [--keep-conflicts]                land a tested commit; exit 2 = retest rebase, 4 = conflict
  status [--all]                              shifts and whether their crews are alive
  down [SHIFT|latest] [--hold|--close]        capture panes, write handover.md, stop the crew; --close (default)
                                              closes its window; --hold keeps the tab open
  cleaner [--dry-run]                         reap dead or finished shifts
  warden [SHIFT] [--dry-run]                  patrol live shifts without teardown
  gaffer [--max-shifts N] [--ticket ID] [--crew NAME] [--repo PATH] [--tick] [--dry-run]
                                              dispatch below the floor concurrency cap
  spawn SHIFT --role ROLE [--cli claude|gemini|codex|copilot] [--crew NAME] [--slot N]
                                              start a session in a free slot of the shift's 1x4 window
  consult SHIFT QUESTION --asg ID             start the reserved Advisor with a durable first assignment
  loop TICKET [TICKET...] [--stall-minutes N] optional batch runner: start, wait for result.json, down --close, next
  loop --project PREFIX [--max N]             same over a project's backlog, lowest number first
  resume [--project PREFIX] [--dry-run]       rerun tickets whose latest shift never reached done (--continue-from it)
  claim SHIFT ROLE PATH...                    claim files before editing; exit 4 if another role holds one
  release SHIFT ROLE [PATH...]                drop those claims, or all of ROLE's when no paths given
  claims SHIFT                                print the shift's claims as JSON
  msg send SHIFT FROM TO --kind K --body TEXT [--asg ID]
                                              store a crew message; prints its header line
  msg sent SHIFT ID                           mark a stored message as sent with SendMessage
  inbox SHIFT ROLE                            unacked inbound, unsent outbound, active assignments
  ack SHIFT ROLE ID                           acknowledge and print the stored body; exit 5 = do not act
  build SHIFT [--cwd DIR] [--cmd 'COMMAND'] [--timeout MIN]
                                              run a build one at a time per folder; evidence in builds/<n>.json
  build --cancel SHIFT N                      kill build N and mark it cancelled
  log SHIFT [--follow] [--since N] [--json]   print the shift bus (bus.jsonl): messages, acks, start..down
  floor say FROM TEXT [--to NAME]             append a message to the machine floor bus
  floor hear ME [--since ID] [--follow]       read floor messages addressed to ME or all

usage: nightshift start [-h] [--prompt-file PROMPT_FILE] [--cwd CWD]
                        [--no-worktree] [--target-branch TARGET_BRANCH]
                        [--continue-from SHIFT_DIR] [--crew CREW]
                        [--crew-file CREW_FILE] [--without ROLE]
                        [--role ROLE=TOOL:MODEL[:REASONING]]
                        [--max-credits N] [--dry-run]
                        [prompt]

Start a Nightshift crew: Claude Foreman, Advisor, Coder and Tester side by
side in one Windows Terminal tab (the default crew; --crew NAME uses
crews/NAME.yaml for other roles and pane counts). The task is saved to
<state_dir>/prompt.txt and given to Foreman only; Coder and Tester send READY
and wait for Foreman to delegate work; the Advisor stays dormant until Foreman
consults it. Git shifts use an isolated worktree; --no-worktree keeps in-place
execution. Each start is a new shift with its own <shift>-foreman /
<shift>-advisor / <shift>-coder / <shift>-tester session names; there is no
restart or resume, and a closed pane is not relaunched. A folder holds one
live shift at a time: start exits with code 3 while another live shift holds
the working folder (nightshift down releases it).

positional arguments:
  prompt                the task for Foreman (quote it; it is treated as plain
                        text), or a ticket ID such as NGH-005: the ticket body
                        becomes the task and its codebase: field the working
                        folder

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --prompt-file PROMPT_FILE
                        read the task from this UTF-8 file instead (safest for
                        text with quotes or & | < > ^ %)
  --cwd CWD             folder the crew works in (default: the ticket
                        codebase, else the current directory)
  --no-worktree         work in place with the existing folder lock
  --target-branch TARGET_BRANCH
                        branch to start from and land onto (repository
                        default, else main)
  --continue-from SHIFT_DIR
                        an earlier shift folder for the same task: its
                        handover.md is appended so the crew carries on
  --crew CREW           crew manifest CREW.yaml, first found in
                        <state root>/crews, <repo>/.nightshift/crews, then the
                        built-in crews/: roles, briefs, colours, counts, model
                        (default: default = one Foreman, one Advisor, one
                        Coder, one Tester); nightshift crews lists them
  --crew-file CREW_FILE
                        use this crew manifest file instead of --crew
  --without ROLE        drop ROLE from the crew (repeatable; not the
                        human_contact role)
  --role ROLE=TOOL:MODEL[:REASONING]
                        run ROLE on TOOL with MODEL and optional reasoning
                        (repeatable)
  --max-credits N       the shift's Copilot credit budget, split across the
                        Copilot panes (replaces the manifest's max_credits)
  --dry-run             print the intended command, roles and prompt as JSON;
                        launch and write nothing

Example: nightshift start "Add a --verbose flag to report.py" | nightshift
start --dry-run --prompt-file task.txt

usage: nightshift status [-h] [--all]

List shifts and whether their crews are alive.

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --all       include shifts whose crew is gone

usage: nightshift down [-h] [--hold | --close] [shift]

Stop a crew: capture each pane, write handover.md, end the sessions and
release the folder lock. --close (default) closes the window; --hold leaves
the tab open. When run from inside the crew (Foreman ending its own shift),
its own process tree is killed last, after the output.

positional arguments:
  shift       shift name, unique suffix, or "latest" (default)

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --hold      leave the Terminal tab open
  --close     close the shift's Terminal window (default)

usage: nightshift spawn [-h] --role ROLE
                        [--cli {claude,gemini,codex,copilot,opencode}]
                        [--crew CREW] [--slot SLOT] [--dry-run]
                        shift

Start a crew session in a free slot of a live shift's own window (2x4/1x4
container, NGH-025): adds the role to crew.json and types the pane wrapper
into that slot's cmd shell. Refused when the window is gone, no slot is free,
or the role is already live. Foreman only.

positional arguments:
  shift                 shift name, unique suffix, or "latest"

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --role ROLE           role label, e.g. Advisor or Coder2 (letters, digits,
                        _)
  --cli {claude,gemini,codex,copilot,opencode}
                        the CLI to run: claude (default), gemini (agy), codex
                        or copilot; opencode is not wired yet. Overrides the
                        tool --crew would give
  --crew CREW           take the role's brief, colour, tool, model, reasoning
                        and account from crews/NAME.yaml instead of the
                        shift's own manifest (e.g. apprentice-codex)
  --slot SLOT           slot number (default: the first free one)
  --dry-run             print the member and the pane command; write, type and
                        start nothing

usage: nightshift consult [-h] --asg ASG shift question

positional arguments:
  shift       shift name, unique suffix, or "latest"
  question    the Foreman question for the Advisor

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --asg ASG   the durable consultation assignment id

usage: nightshift loop [-h] [--project PREFIX] [--max N] [--cwd CWD]
                       [--stall-minutes STALL_MINUTES] [--retries RETRIES]
                       [--notify] [--no-notify]
                       [tickets ...]

Run tickets one per shift: start a crew, wait for result.json (or a stall),
tear the shift down, note the ticket, continue. Stops at the first
blocked/stalled/died shift so a human can look. With --project PREFIX [--max
N], works that project's backlog tickets (lowest number first, needs-human
skipped) and moves each to in-progress when its shift starts.

positional arguments:
  tickets               ticket IDs, worked in order

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --project PREFIX      work this project's backlog instead of listed tickets
  --max N               work at most N tickets
  --cwd CWD             working folder for every shift (default: each ticket
                        codebase)
  --stall-minutes STALL_MINUTES
  --retries RETRIES     rerun a ticket this many times after its crew dies or
                        stalls (default 2)
  --notify              email the owner via Mailkeep when the loop halts or
                        finishes
  --no-notify           do not email the owner (default)

usage: nightshift resume [-h] [--project PREFIX] [--dry-run]
                         [--stall-minutes STALL_MINUTES] [--notify]
                         [--no-notify]

Rerun every ticket whose latest shift never reached done (crew died, stalled,
blocked or was stopped), each continuing from that shift's handover. Done and
still-running tickets are skipped. Locks held by dead shifts are cleared
first. Prints the plan as JSON.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

shift's isolated git worktree (or the caller's directory with --no-worktree) in Claude's auto permission

resume; a closed pane is not relaunched. `start --dry-run` prints the plan as

in the first slots and plain cmd shells in the rest (each records <state_dir>/slots/<N>.json); the launcher exits once every pane and slot has

<state_dir>/<Role>.json records pid, name, peer and model. There is no restart or
resume; a closed pane is not relaunched. `start --dry-run` prints the plan as
JSON without launching or writing anything.

in the first slots and plain cmd shells in the rest (each records <state_dir>/slots/<N>.json); the launcher exits once every pane and slot has

repository lock during `land`; direct and non-git working folders hold one live shift at a time.
